description: A curated Reactome biochemical reaction with inputs and outputs. A reaction directly contained in several pathways is represented by one node.

common_properties.name: identifier
common_properties.description: Reactome stable ID prefixed with reactome:, for example reactome:R-HSA-389357.

common_properties.name: reactome_id
common_properties.description: Bare Reactome stable ID, for example R-HSA-389357.

common_properties.name: name
common_properties.description: Reactome display name; the bare stable ID is used when a display name is missing.

common_properties.name: version
common_properties.description: Reactome release number in which the reaction was last seen.

common_properties.name: sources
common_properties.description: Data source contributing the reaction: Reactome.

common_properties.name: last_updated
common_properties.description: Time the reaction record was created or last changed in SPOKE.

source_contributions.scope: Biochemical reactions directly contained in the human Reactome pathway hierarchies rooted at R-HSA-162582 (Signaling Pathways, historically Signal Transduction), R-HSA-168256 (Immune System), and R-HSA-5663202 (Diseases of signal transduction by growth factor receptors and second messengers), including all descendant pathways. Degradation and template-reaction events are excluded.
source_contributions.description: The source is the human BioPAX Level 3 export. Reaction membership connects a reaction to each pathway that directly contains it. Participant relationships represent inputs and outputs without distinguishing their roles; catalysts and regulators are excluded. Alternative entity sets are not expanded into their members. Summaries, literature references, cellular compartments, stoichiometry, EC numbers, catalysis and regulation relationships are not represented.

properties.name: synonyms
properties.description: Reactome alternate names, excluding names equal to the display name without regard to case. Duplicate alternate names are compared without regard to case, retaining the first spelling.
